rows.summary: The report mislabels the already-completed 25 September MACD bullish crossover as a pending upgrade trigger, so its adopted two-of-three add rule is already satisfied while the call says add nothing. Its core valuation and growth figures (9.3% revenue CAGR, 5.3x PEG, '51x forward', ~20% compression downside) are miscomputed or mislabelled. It also misclassifies Costco as Consumer Discretionary, names a wrong next earnings event, ignores the stock sitting 15.5% below its 52-week high, and leans on fabricated sector and membership figures, so it is not fit for publication..

The Underweight ruling rests on a bear EPS calculation that applies net margin to gross profit ($0.27) and on comparing a quarterly EPS of $0.63 with an annual target, both of which are wrong. RSI 33 is misread as oversold, MACD convergence is misdescribed as widening, the fundamentals are a quarter stale with duplicated balance-sheet data, the price target is underived, and the digest is missing.

The Hold ruling rests on a valuation argument that divides quarterly normalized EPS into price as if annual, turning ~12x into '47-51x'. The bear case attributes Q2 earnings to a September volatility spike and wrongly places price below the 200-day SMA. A sub-ATR stop, invented deposit-cost and peer-multiple figures, and numerous arithmetic slips leave the report unfit for publication without substantial rework.

The report's core bearish case rests on misread inputs. It treats an operating loss as operating cash flow, computes runway on cash alone despite large investment holdings, presents an already-occurred MACD bearish crossover as a future exit trigger, and calls a seasonal, YoY-flat revenue line 'shrinking'. Add a $205 price target above the current price on an Underweight call, exit levels mislabeled against the 10-day EMA, and pervasive arithmetic and attribution slips, and it is not fit for publication.

The price-derived technicals are mostly accurate, but the report misstates capex intensity (34.9% of revenue, not 9.2%), gets the FCF decline wrong, misreads a freshly bullish MACD histogram as compressing, and treats unreported Q1 FY2027 results as in hand. The ruling rests on invented scenario probabilities, a 'second straight year' of margin compression that its own data contradicts, and an entry style that conflicts with the no-new-money decision, so it is not fit to publish.

The headline Hold is reasonable, but the supporting case rests on a share-count error that inflates the FCF yield 8x, an invented 26x forward P/E, fabricated peer comparables, and a misread MACD figure turned into a nonsensical '86% collapse' that the ruling repeats. Price-level facts are mostly right in the digest, but the cross-section inconsistencies, the mid-cap mislabel, the ignored 52-week high, and agent-name/emoji presentation mean it needs substantial rework before publication.

The price-derived technicals are mostly accurate against the computed facts. However, the report's core fundamentals are misread: cumulative or trailing OCF is presented as quarterly, sequential growth as YoY, and liabilities/equity as D/E. Valuation and scenario math is broken (a 1.8x P/E, conflicting market caps, an inflated +19% expected value), the $265 target is underived, and the stop coincides with the add level, so the Overweight call is not publishable as written.

The technical figures match the computed price facts, but the fundamental core does not hold. The 1.35x dividend coverage rests on an invented ~400M share count that the report's own EPS data contradicts (implying coverage below 1x), and the $7.6B investing figure likely double-counts YTD cash flows. Mislabelled 'debt-to-equity', a three-quarter decline called quarterly, an inaccurate qualified-dividend claim, and a miscalculated expected-value synthesis feed directly into the ruling, bull/bear points and exit triggers, alongside many minor arithmetic slips and agent-name leaks.

Most price facts and the core fundamental arithmetic reconcile, but the report rests on a mislabelled 'debt-to-equity' (actually liabilities-to-equity) and an invented $120 rival bid in a key point. It also has a price target borrowed from Stifel without derivation and conflicting stop levels, one inside a single ATR. Numerous secondary slips undermine confidence: the 7.1% vs 9.0% EMA gap, '10-15% upside' to an $80 target, inconsistent decline percentages, a weekend close date, and a self-contradictory Synaptics narrative.

The ruling rests on a miscomputed opex-to-gross-profit ratio (5.5x, not 2.4x) and an inconsistent capital-raised figure ($1.8B vs $2.8B). It also treats a post-quarter $56M order as 67% of Q2 revenue, while runway is stated three different ways across sections. The trade plan is structurally unsound: the price target is just the stop level, the stop sits on the wrong side for a short and inside one ATR, and the technical section misreads the MACD crossover and the price-versus-EMA relationship.)

The headline price facts (moving averages, RSI, MACD, 52-week high) are correctly stated. However, the report carries load-bearing problems: an underived $480 target below spot on a Hold, invented fundamentals (backlog through 2027, FCF yield) used in the bull and bear key points, a quarterly GDP figure misread as annual, and no mention of the mid-October earnings release inside its own review window. Numerous secondary slips in the technical section (a mislabeled 200-day SMA, a stop described as below the 10-day EMA when it is above, wrong RSI arithmetic, an inconsistent 200-day gap) and internal agent names in reader-facing text add to the case against publication.

The report gets the basic moving-average, RSI and 52-week figures right. But its decision rests on a misread MACD (claiming no bearish crossover when one occurred on 2026-09-16), an invented market cap and FCF yield that conflict across sections, and an inverted cash-flow-versus-revenue claim in a bull key point. The ruling's dividend-carry tie-break is unsupported and logically flawed, and an exit trigger is conditioned on an event that already happened, so it is not fit to publish without substantive rework.
